Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screen-less fitness tracker, similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. Having used WHOOP for the past six months, I do think this is a good idea, but there are a few areas where I hope Apple can do better.

Since the product is still in early development, we don't yet know the specific design of Apple's screen-less fitness tracker. It's unlikely to launch until at least 2028. Bloomberg described it as "a thin fabric band with a built-in sensor computing module."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase on a promotional offer, letting Sapphire cardholders get a WHOOP at a discount or for free, and I took advantage of it. I've been using WHOOP since then, though I've never fully committed to it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection will never be perfect, and I find it a hassle to have to pull out my phone to log a workout, either before or after the fact. With Apple Watch, you just start the workout from the watch face, and WHOOP can sync the timing from Apple Health. That's the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

If I'm heading to the gym for a workout, pulling out my phone is acceptable, but for a casual bike ride or walk, I'd rather not bother with my phone.

So for Apple's screen-less fitness tracker, I'd love to see some kind of button plus indicator light combo that lets you start and stop workouts. You'd still need your phone to categorise the activity afterwards, but I'd rather do that later than in the moment. Apple could also develop categorisation models based on certain factors.

Summary

If Apple can successfully create a screen-less fitness tracker that doesn't feel like a hassle and doesn't require your phone, I think it would be very appealing. This kind of design has many advantages, including comfort to wear, longer battery life, and the ability to be worn alongside a traditional watch.

Personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I do prefer just wearing a smartwatch, even if it means sacrificing battery life. I understand some people want a screen-less design so they won't be distracted, but for me, I just turn on Do Not Disturb mode on my watch and that solves it.

What do you think about Apple developing a screen-less fitness tracker? What price would it take for you to buy one? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
